summary: Moala Airport (MFJ) is a small domestic airstrip serving Moala Island, part of Fiji's remote Lau Islands group in the eastern maritime region of the country. The airport primarily handles inter-island flights operated by Fiji Link, connecting the island's small communities to the main island of Viti Levu. Its modest infrastructure reflects the low-volume, essential lifeline role it plays for residents of this isolated part of Fiji.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Moala Airport?
A: Fiji Link, the domestic subsidiary of Fiji Airways, operates scheduled services connecting Moala to Nausori Airport near Suva on Viti Levu.

Q: How far is Moala Airport from the main settlement?
A: The airstrip is located on the island with road access to nearby villages, though travel times depend on the local road conditions and weather.

Q: Are there facilities at the terminal?
A: The terminal is very basic, typical of Fiji's outer island airstrips, with limited shelter and minimal passenger amenities.

Q: How often do flights operate to Moala?
A: Scheduled flights are infrequent, typically only a few times per week, and schedules can change with weather and demand.
transport_tips: There is no public bus service; arrange ground transport in advance through your accommodation or the local carrier. The small terminal area offers minimal services, so plan for a short walk or pre-arranged pickup after landing. Be prepared for flexible scheduling, as flights to the Lau Islands can be delayed or rescheduled due to weather conditions.
local_tip: Pack light and bring any essentials from Suva, as shops on Moala Island have limited stock and supply ships are infrequent.
